drivingQuestion: How can wine asparagus be good for the intestines when the ללע״ט baraita says wine is harmful to them?
outcomeNote: the contradiction is resolved by an oqimta: the intestine-friendly baraita speaks of old wine, as the Nedarim mishna shows

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִסְפָּרָגוֹס — יָפֶה לַלֵּב וְטוֹב לָעֵינַיִם, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן לִבְנֵי מֵעַיִם. וְהָרָגִיל בּוֹ — יָפֶה לְכׇל גּוּפוֹ. וְהַמִּשְׁתַּכֵּר הֵימֶנּוּ — קָשֶׁה לְכׇל גּוּפוֹ.
segments.en: Tangential to the laws concerning wine that the Gemara cited earlier, «the Sages taught: Asparagus,» wine or other alcoholic beverages that they were accustomed to drink early in the morning before eating, «is agreeable for the heart and beneficial for the eyes, and all the more so for the intestines. And» in extolling the virtues of this drink, the Gemara says: «One who is accustomed to» drink it, «it is agreeable for his entire body.» However, one must be careful, as «one who» drinks excessively and «becomes drunk, it is harmful for his entire body.»

segments.he: מִדְּקָתָנֵי יָפֶה לַלֵּב, מִכְּלָל דִּבְחַמְרָא עָסְקִינַן, וְקָתָנֵי: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן לִבְנֵי מֵעַיִם. וְהָתַנְיָא: לְלַעַ״ט — יָפֶה, לְרָמַ״ת — קָשֶׁה!
segments.en: The Gemara discusses this: «From the fact that it was taught» that asparagus is «agreeable for the heart,» it may be inferred that «we are dealing with» asparagus made from «wine,» which is known to be agreeable for the heart. «And we learned: And all the more so,» asparagus is «beneficial for the intestines. Wasn’t it taught» in a baraita: «For L-E-T,» which is an acronym for lev, heart; einayim, eyes; teḥol, spleen, «it is beneficial,» but «for R-M-T,» rosh, head; me’ayim, intestines; taḥtoniot, hemorrhoids, «it is harmful.» Apparently, asparagus is harmful for one’s intestines.

segments.he: כִּי תַּנְיָא הַהִיא, בִּמְיוּשָּׁן. כְּדִתְנַן: קֻוֽנָּם יַיִן שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם, שֶׁהַיַּיִן קָשֶׁה לִבְנֵי מֵעַיִם. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא מְיוּשָּׁן יָפֶה הוּא לִבְנֵי מֵעַיִם! וְשָׁתַק — אָסוּר בְּחָדָשׁ, וּמוּתָּר בִּמְיוּשָּׁן. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «That» baraita, in which «it was taught» that asparagus is beneficial to one’s intestines, refers to asparagus made «with old» wine. «As we learned» in the mishna concerning the laws of vows that one who vowed: «Wine is konam for me to taste because it is harmful to the intestines, and» those who heard him «said to him: But isn’t old» wine «beneficial to the intestines? If he was silent» and did not argue the point, he is «forbidden» to drink «new» wine because of his vow, «but he is permitted» to drink «old» wine. «Conclude from this» that old wine is beneficial for the intestines.
